analysis.investment_thesis: Flywings scores well on return on capital (ROCE 25%) but fails the Magic Formula's valuation test — at P/E 17, the implied earnings yield of ~5.9% is far below the 12%+ threshold I require for a compelling buy. One leg of the Magic Formula is solid; the other is not.
key_strengths: ROCE of 25% clears Greenblatt's 'excellent business' threshold (>25%), suggesting capital-efficient operations
Regulated aviation simulator niche creates meaningful barriers to entry for a micro-cap
Promoter holding at 59.87% with FII+DII at ~15% combined signals some institutional conviction
key_risks: Earnings yield ~5.9% (1/P/E proxy) is well below Magic Formula's 12% minimum — not cheap
Micro-cap at INR 192 Cr with very limited public data — EBIT, debt, and EV unknown, so full Magic Formula cannot be computed
Aviation simulators are capital-intensive assets; any debt load would compress the true earnings yield further
red_flags: Insufficient data: no revenue, EBIT, or balance sheet figures — Magic Formula cannot be fully computed
At P/E 17, the stock is priced for quality but not at a bargain — violates the 'cheap AND good' requirement
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on available data: ROCE of 25% clears my 'excellent business' bar, suggesting the company earns strong returns on its deployed capital — likely driven by the regulated, high-barrier nature of aviation simulator certification. However, the valuation leg fails badly. Using P/E 17 as a proxy for earnings yield gives ~5.9%, versus my minimum threshold of 12%. Even being generous — assuming zero debt so EV ≈ market cap — the stock is priced at more than 16x earnings with no margin of safety.

The bigger problem is data insufficiency. With no EBIT, no debt schedule, and no revenue growth disclosed, I cannot run a clean Magic Formula ranking. For a INR 192 Cr micro-cap in a niche aviation training business, that opacity is a real concern. The business may well be good — but 'good' at 17x earnings is not what I buy. I need a company to be both a good business AND cheap. This one is only halfway there at best. Wait for a meaningful price pullback to ~P/E 10-11 (earnings yield ~9-10%) before revisiting.
